The Built-in Templates section is expanded by default while there are no saved automations. Tab to a template and press Enter or Space to open a New automation dialog with an editable name, prompt, and schedule.

For saved automations, Tab to a card's Edit control and action buttons. Use Left Arrow and Right Arrow to move between Run now and More Actions. Press Enter or Space to activate a control. Edit, or clicking anywhere else on the card, opens the automation dialog. More Actions opens the automation menu. Duplicate opens a prefilled New automation dialog for portable schedules and is unavailable for event-triggered automations. Disable prevents future runs, and Delete asks for confirmation. Run now requests execution from the selected provider when available.

When creating an automation and cloud automations are enabled, a Run in the cloud switch, described as Preview, follows the Name field; press Space to turn it on or off. If cloud automations cannot be reached when you turn it on, the switch turns back off and a message asks you to try again in a few moments. When it is on, Cloud is the agent and the workspace picker lists Git-backed workspaces. Only GitHub repositories that support cloud automation management can be selected; unavailable repositories are announced with the reason. Choose Add repository to search for a repository or paste its URL. A matching local folder is retained. If cloud automations become unavailable while the switch is on, Cloud stays selected and Create is unavailable until they return or, for a new automation, you turn the switch off. Turning the switch off restores the previous local workspace and agent, or otherwise selects Copilot when it is available. Cloud models are configured in the prompt section. In the Tools section, the button shows All tools allowed or the number of tools allowed. Activate it to open a searchable checklist of the tools GitHub offers, grouped by category. Categories start collapsed; use Right Arrow to expand one. Press Space to toggle a tool or category. Each change applies immediately to the dialog; Enter or Escape closes the checklist without discarding changes. Save or Create saves the automation. New automations start with every listed tool selected. While the list loads the button is unavailable, and if it cannot be loaded a Retry button appears. Trigger follows the tools controls. Scheduled triggers display local time; GitHub stores a fixed UTC schedule, so the local run time may shift when daylight saving time changes. When editing a cloud automation, the switch and workspace picker are disabled because changing the repository or provider requires duplication. Editing preserves enabled state; enable or disable an automation from its card.

Cloud history shows the repository, status, and last updated time even when no local session is available. When a cloud run has a session on GitHub that is not yet loaded in VS Code, click its row, or Tab to its title and press Enter or Space, to open that exact session. Tab to a row's toolbar and use Left Arrow and Right Arrow to reach Open on GitHub and Stop when supported. Archive or Mark as Done is unavailable until the cloud run and its conversation have finished. It changes local session state, not the task on GitHub. Stop requests remote cancellation; the status changes when GitHub reports it. Follow-up requests show conversation progress and restart bounded history discovery. Use Refresh in the view header to reload definitions and history. Active cloud runs refresh every 15 seconds without moving the history rows; idle definitions do not poll.

In the automation dialog, Target controls are above the prompt. Agent and model pickers are inside the prompt input, and execution mode and permission controls are below it. Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move between fields and pickers. When creating an automation, you only need to enter a prompt. An empty name is derived from the prompt, and the target defaults to No workspace unless one is already supplied. An available Agent Host that supports the target is still required.

For Cloud automations, the Trigger picker combines Weekly, Daily, Hourly, Issue, Pull Request, and Manual in one control. Issue and Pull Request are offered when their events are available to your account. Scheduled triggers show time and day controls as applicable. Event appears to the right of Trigger, in the same position as Time for a schedule. Issue uses one Event. For Pull Request, activate the Event button to open a searchable checklist. Use Up Arrow and Down Arrow to navigate and Space to select events; at least one stays selected. Enter or Escape closes the checklist. Required event fields appear directly below the Trigger and Event row. Create remains unavailable until they are completed, and its hover explains what is missing. Expand Advanced below them to configure optional filters and Include activity from users without write access to this repository. When selected events support the same filter, such as Query or Paths, it appears once and applies to each of those events. Labels, assignees and changed paths accept comma-separated values; paths use gitignore patterns. Query filters the target and Comment text filters a comment's body. Review states are checkboxes. Include activity from users without write access to this repository starts on; turn it off to require write access to trigger the automation. Unsupported or mixed triggers are read-only with Open on GitHub; editing other fields keeps the saved triggers. Event automations run from GitHub events rather than Run now.
When repository settings disallow activity from users without write access, that option is turned off and unavailable, with the explanation Disabled by your repository settings.
For cloud automation cards, More Actions also offers Open on GitHub to open the automation's details in your browser.

Run history is grouped by date. While a run is waiting for its session, a lightweight row shows the automation name with a Working... description. Once the session is available, use Up Arrow and Down Arrow to navigate the Sessions list, Enter to open, and Tab to reach Stop, the configured Archive or Mark as Done action, or Delete when available. Open a row's context menu, for example with Shift+F10, to rename it, change its active or read state, or delete it. Delete permanently deletes the session and removes it from run history after confirmation.
You are in the Automations view. It contains available automation cards followed by run history. Loading, unavailable, and error messages indicate that the catalogue may be incomplete.

Saved cards are grouped under collapsible Your automations and Shared automations sections. Press Enter or Space on a section header to expand or collapse it. The Shared automations info icon explains who can view and edit those automations. Cloud creation has an Owner control after Tools. Use the arrow keys to choose Only me or Repository; Only me is the default. Ownership cannot be changed when editing. Repository readers can view Shared automations; writers can manage them. The Templates from Plugins section is available whenever enabled plugins provide templates. Press Enter or Space on its disclosure control to expand or collapse it. A blue marker indicates templates added since the section was last expanded. Plugin templates start disabled.

Explore the codebase and report verified, reproducible bugs.

Explore this codebase and find concrete, reproducible bugs.

Read the repository guidance and understand the architecture before choosing a focused area to investigate, such as recent changes, complex state transitions, or error handling. Trace suspected problems through callers and existing tests. Use the smallest relevant tests or a minimal reproduction to verify behavior, and distinguish confirmed bugs from hypotheses. Avoid style-only suggestions and speculative findings.

Report high-confidence, actionable bugs with severity, file and line references, a triggering scenario, expected versus actual behavior, and supporting test or reproduction results. Suggest a focused fix for each finding without modifying repository files or committing changes. State what you explored, any validation limitations, and when no confirmed bugs were found.
Triage my GitHub repositories' issues using their precedents.

Triage my GitHub repositories' issues using existing repository precedents.

Use the authenticated GitHub account to find my repositories, prioritizing active repositories and new or untriaged issues. For each repository, read its contribution guidelines, issue templates, existing labels, and comparable issues with maintainer decisions. Learn each repository's conventions separately before making recommendations.

Produce a report grouped by repository. Link to each issue, recommend existing labels, identify likely duplicates, and draft a reply when useful. Cite prior issues, pull requests, or maintainer comments supporting each recommendation. Flag uncertainty or missing precedent rather than inventing a rule. Do not apply labels, post comments, close issues, or make other GitHub changes. State which repositories and issues were reviewed and any access limitations.
Pull the latest main and summarize new commits.

Pull the latest main and summarize the commits that were pulled.

Inspect this repository's current branch, working tree, and configured remotes. Resolve the remote for main from the repository configuration rather than assuming origin. Record HEAD, then pull that remote's main into the current checkout using --ff-only. Proceed only with a clean working tree and a fast-forward update. If the remote is ambiguous, main is missing, or the update is blocked, stop and explain why. Do not switch branches, stash or discard local changes, rebase, or force an update.

Compare the starting and ending HEAD and summarize only newly pulled commits, grouped by theme. Highlight user-visible changes, bug fixes, breaking changes, and follow-up actions. Include commit links and related pull requests when available. If no commits were pulled, say so.

When disabled, you start and end each turn manually, and ending the turn sends it. Turns are not ended automatically on trailing silence or a stop phrase unless {0} or {1} is explicitly configured.

The language used for speech recognition, dictation, and spoken responses. The selectable languages support native voice output. Automatic uses the configured display language for speech recognition and dictation when supported; otherwise, it follows the system or browser locale. English voice output is used when the detected language does not support native voice output. Changing this while voice mode is connected takes effect immediately.

Show your speech as a live, word-by-word transcript while you are speaking. When disabled, your transcript appears only once you finish speaking. Requires `#agents.voice.showTranscript#` to be enabled to be visible.

Share a bounded briefing of tracked sessions and the active chat's recent conversation with OpenAI BYOK Voice Mode, so it can answer session status questions directly. This includes session titles, response summaries, pending prompt details, the selected model, and attachment names, but not attachment contents. Disable to restore input-only context. Changes take effect when Voice Mode reconnects.
Controls whether the Voice Mode button is shown in the chat input. When hidden, Voice Mode can still be started with its keyboard shortcut.
Show the voice transcript overlay in the chat input area while voice mode is active. Enable this to read responses as text when `#agents.voice.speakResponses#` is disabled.
When enabled, the assistant reads responses aloud. When disabled, responses are not spoken; enable `#agents.voice.showTranscript#` to read them as a text transcript instead.

Trailing silence in milliseconds before the backend ends the turn automatically. Set to `-1` to disable ending the turn on silence, in which case the turn ends only via a stop phrase ({0}) or manually. When enabled, the backend clamps this to its supported range (currently 200-5000 ms) and is the source of truth. When hands-free mode ({1}) is disabled, the turn is not ended on silence by default unless this setting is explicitly configured, so you keep manual control over when a turn is sent.
Do not end the turn on trailing silence.

Phrases that end the turn when spoken at the end of an utterance. Leave empty to disable ending the turn on a stop phrase, in which case the turn ends only on trailing silence ({0}) or manually. The backend strips the matched phrase from the transcript before it reaches the agent. When hands-free mode ({1}) is disabled, stop phrases do not end the turn by default unless this setting is explicitly configured, so you keep manual control over when a turn is sent.

The OpenAI live model ID to use for Voice Mode with your configured API key. Add the key in Models Management. Voice Mode uses this model when client BYOK is allowed and the key has access to it; leave empty to use the hosted voice model, which requires a paid Copilot plan.

The voice used when the assistant reads responses aloud. Changing this while voice mode is connected takes effect immediately. Use [Voice Mode instructions](command:{0}) to customize Voice Mode behavior and terminology.

When an agent session exposes approval presets, use Tab to reach the Approvals picker and choose how it handles workspace access, commands, and the internet.

When your organization disables Claude or Codex, their Agent Host conversations remain listed and read-only. If your organization also requires the new Copilot experience, an open, idle conversation automatically moves to Copilot with its title, history, and draft. Nothing is sent automatically. The original is archived only after the copy opens and other conversations in its session can still be reached. Opening an archived original does not move it again. If moving needs a workspace or trust decision, or fails, use Tab to focus Continue in Copilot in the banner, then press Enter or Space. This action reopens an existing copy when available. Subagent chats require the manual action. For a managed checkout, choose an independent workspace; uncommitted files stay in the original checkout. If saved history cannot load, use Retry in the error banner.

When a sandbox dependency warning appears above the input, use Tab to reach Troubleshooting Guide or, when permitted, Disable Sandboxing. Press Enter or Space to activate the button. Disable Sandboxing turns sandboxing off for this session and in settings; organization policy still applies.
In Copilot agent-host sessions, use /sandbox policy to view the effective sandbox policy. In the response, use Tab to focus Open Sandbox Policy and Enter to open the formatted report.

A running Agent Host chat may show an invitation to continue or view your sessions in the Agents Window. Only one invitation is shown across editor windows at a time. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach its action, Don't Show Again, or Dismiss notification. The action opens the Agents Window and highlights this session's row in the sessions list when onboarding is enabled. By default, it also opens this chat. Choose Next to highlight the New Session button, which you can activate to start another task. Disable chat.agentsWindowBanner.revealCurrentSession to open the New Session view instead and only highlight the invited session's row. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to move between the tour actions and any interactive highlighted control. Choose Understood to finish the tour, or press Escape to dismiss it. Sending another message or completing a task does not dismiss the invitation. It is temporarily hidden while the session needs attention. Dismiss notification snoozes invitations until you have created five more Agent Host sessions in editor windows and at least 24 hours have passed since the invitation appeared. Don't Show Again turns off all future Agents Window invitations.
Chat responses will be announced as they come in. A response will indicate the number of code blocks, if any, and then the rest of the response.

Artifact actions appear as collapsed request cards with an action and resource label. Use Tab to reach the card and Enter or Space to expand it. The details are a snapshot from when the action started. Use arrow keys within a details list and Enter to open an item. Agent Message switches between these details and the full prompt. Open the accessible view{0} while the request is focused to read its snapshot as text.
To inspect an inline attachment reference, place the cursor on it and invoke Show or Focus Hover{0}. Image references include a preview, while file and folder references include their path.
To mention an attached context item at a specific position without removing it from the attached context, type # or @ and select the attachment from the suggestions.
Long pasted text, including single-line text, is stored as an attached text item and replaced in the input with a numbered inline reference.
To remove attached contexts, focus an attachment and press Delete or Backspace.

Type /blobby to unlock the True Name achievement without sending a chat request. If Blobby is off, the command turns it on; if it is already on, it opens the Color tab in Customize Blobby. Change Color in the pet's context menu always opens Color, where Stable and Insiders are free choices. True Name unlocks solid presets and custom colors; activating that achievement also opens Color. Use the color picker or enter an opaque hex color such as #ff8800, then activate Apply Color. Unapplied custom colors are discarded when you leave the tab or close the modal.

In a conversation that supports side chats, type /btw followed by a question to open a side chat with the prior conversation as context. You can ask while a response is in progress without stopping it.

In local Copilot agent-host sessions with chat.canvases.enabled turned on, Add Context includes Canvas immediately after Sessions. Open Canvas to choose a registered or closed canvas by name. Activating one opens or refocuses its tab; it does not attach anything to the prompt.

When {0} is enabled, typing in a new Cloud chat, with or without a repository, can prepare cloud resources in the background. Your message is not sent and no conversation is added to the session list until you press Send. Send waits for pending preparation and reuses it when possible, otherwise it can continue without early preparation. While the window is running, VS Code attempts to release unused preparation after five minutes, when you change repositories, or when you turn the setting off.

If cloud session creation or connection fails, the current response offers Show Details. Use Tab to focus Show Details and Enter or Space to open a dialog with the failed step and available request details. Opening details does not sign in or retry the request. As with other response buttons, Show Details is unavailable after the conversation is restored.

A ChatGPT limit suggestion may offer Continue with Copilot. If the eligible Codex session is not active, the guide highlights its row in the Sessions list. Activate Open Session in the guide or open the row using the list's usual keyboard shortcut: by default, Command+Down Arrow on macOS or Enter on Windows and Linux. The next step opens its model picker with a matching Copilot model in the search. Activate Use Copilot in the guide or use Up and Down Arrow and Enter in the picker to select the Copilot model. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach the guide's buttons and Enter or Space to activate them. An already-active eligible session goes directly to the picker. End Tour or Escape cancels the remaining guidance; it does not undo a model selection.

When completed response collapsing is enabled, the final response remains visible while earlier work is collapsed. Use Tab to focus the work disclosure and press Enter or Space to show or hide that work. With persistent progress enabled, a separate file changes button shows lines added and deleted when the collapsed work includes edits. Activate it to open those file changes without expanding the work.

Depending on the active experiment, a new Copilot harness chat may show an introduction to the new Copilot experience when the session starts or after the first request is submitted. Once shown, sending messages does not dismiss it. Use Tab to reach let us know, Learn More, Got it!, or Not Helpful. Learn More opens documentation without hiding the introduction. Got it! and Not Helpful turn off future introductions.

When workspace customizations need an update, a notice above the new-chat input shows how many need attention. Use Tab to reach Review Migrations and open the Migrations page. Dismiss Migration Notice for This Workspace hides the notice for that workspace, including after restarting, and returns focus to the input. The Customizations toolbar button also announces when migrations are available.
The chat view is a persistent interface that also supports navigating suggested follow-up questions, while the quick chat view is a transient interface for making and viewing requests.
The quick chat view is a transient interface for making and viewing requests, while the panel chat view is a persistent interface that also supports navigating suggested follow-up questions.

The editor window uses the same compact Artifacts pill as the Agents Window, rather than an expanded list above the input. Generated images appear automatically. In a subagent chat, the Artifacts pill shows that chat's transcript artifacts without the parent session's metadata. A single file pill opens directly; multiple artifacts open a dropdown with a Generated Images section. Use the pill's hover or context menu, or a dropdown row's actions, to save an artifact or copy its path.

In local Copilot agent-host sessions with chat.canvases.enabled turned on, a Canvas submenu appears in the final section of the New Chat menu, and the chat's open canvases appear in their own pill in the main window. Open the Canvas submenu to choose a registered or closed canvas by name. Use Up and Down Arrow, Right Arrow, and Enter to navigate the menus and open or refocus a canvas. A single canvas in the pill shows its title and opens directly; multiple canvases show a count and open a picker. Activating a canvas focuses its tab beside the chat, or reopens it if it was closed. To close a canvas rather than only its tab, use Close Canvas: the X on a canvas pill or picker row, or the pill's context menu. Closing ends the canvas and notifies the extension that provides it.

For an Agent Host chat editor, open the editor tab context menu and choose Copy Link to copy a session URL that renders as a session link in Markdown. Selecting multiple chat tabs copies one link per line.
The agent sessions filter includes an External submenu. Use it to choose whether external sessions from another application are shown for the last 24 hours, the last 7 days, always, or not at all.

File change summaries show the total files, additions, and deletions. Focus the disclosure and press Enter or Space to show or hide the individual files. Focus an additions and deletions label and press Enter or Space to open the changes in a diff editor.
To search the chat transcript, invoke Find in Chat{0}. Find Next{1} and Find Previous{2} move between results, scrolling each one into view.
To focus the last chat terminal that ran a tool, invoke the Focus Most Recent Chat Terminal command{0}.
To focus the output from the last chat terminal tool, invoke the Focus Most Recent Chat Terminal Output command{0}.
When a tip, notification or introduction appears above the input, toggle focus between it and the chat input{0}.
When a chat question appears, toggle focus between the question and the chat input{0}.

In an Agent Host chat that supports forking, type /fork to create a forked chat beside the current one. Add a title after /fork to name it, or type /fork prompt followed by a prompt to also send that prompt in the new chat.
Selecting the /fork title or /fork prompt completion inserts the command without submitting it. The title and prompt hints shown after the command are suggestions and are not part of your input.

Each consecutive batch of image-generation calls has its own preview in conversation order. Select any thumbnail, including one still generating, to show its image or progress and its tool dropdown above the preview. Use Tab to focus the selected thumbnail, then Left or Right Arrow, Home, or End to select another image or its progress. Expand the selected tool dropdown to inspect its prompt and output, including timing and size. The selected thumbnail has a highlighted border. The thumbnail row follows the selected preview's size. Generating images show only the compact glyph band, while cancelled or failed images show their status in the tool dropdown without an empty preview. The Image batch status below the thumbnails shows how many images are ready out of the total, along with any that need attention, failed, or were cancelled. Later results arrive without changing your selection, and only the selected preview animates. Focus the main image and press Enter to open the carousel. Approval and authentication requests remain visible even when another image is selected.

Use the download action beside the Image batch status to save all currently ready images as a ZIP archive. Use Tab to reach it and Enter or Space to download. The action is unavailable until an image is ready and while a download is in progress. Only images ready when you start the download are included; failed, cancelled, and pending images are not included.
Stopping image generation shows Image generation cancelled, not a generation error. Cancelled image tools keep their cancelled status when you reopen the chat.

Generated images also appear in artifacts. When Images Preview is enabled for chat, opening an image lets you browse generated images, user-attached images, and images shown in responses from the same conversation. Use the Left and Right Arrow keys to move between images.

Expand a completed image-generation dropdown to inspect its duration, total image byte size, and tokens. A dash means the value was not reported; token usage is not yet available. Generated image downloads include a stable hash suffix so different images have distinct filenames.

Image-generation tool entries, previews, and batch counts stay hidden while the model assembles the tool arguments. If approval is required, the confirmation is the first tool UI shown. Generating image, the glyph animation, painting progress phrases, and the painting pet start only when the tool executes, after any required confirmation. Confirmation and authentication waits pause image-generation progress.

Image generation appears separately from thinking and tool-call groups. Copilot and Codex agent sessions share this presentation. Completed steps collapse only before the first image-generation tool, keeping image tools in their original position. While generation runs, expand the tool dropdown to inspect the submitted prompt. Its title says Generating image with the image model when the model is available, and does not shimmer. The image model can differ from the selected conversation model. A compact decorative band of shifting glyphs remains visible below the dropdown and reveals a single image when its bytes are available. The animation does not indicate a percentage complete and stays still when reduced motion is enabled or a high contrast theme is active. The reveal is skipped in those modes and when reopening a chat. Only the persistent progress line rotates through painting-themed phrases, without repeatedly announcing them. These phrases are decorative, not individual generation stages. Use Tab to focus the dropdown and Enter or Space to expand or collapse it. Successful generation shows the Generated image dropdown, including the image model when available, with a single image below it even when collapsed. If generation fails, the Generated image failed row can be expanded to inspect the error. Completed and failed image tools keep their final status when you reopen the chat. Image previews start loading as soon as generation succeeds, even if the response is still in progress. A preview is marked as busy while its bytes load. Unable to load image indicates a problem loading the preview, not a failed generation. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to focus an image and Enter to open it. Use the Save action to the right of the image to save generated images.
Once an image is ready, the preview begins resizing immediately, followed by the glyph-to-image reveal. Reduced motion and high contrast skip this transition.

After you switch from Copilot to Local, a feedback survey may appear above the chat input. Use Shift+Tab to reach it. Use Up and Down Arrow to choose why you switched, then press Enter or Space to submit. Dismiss Survey or Escape closes the survey. After submission, a message confirms that your feedback was recorded. Use Tab to reach Share it on GitHub to provide specific feedback in a GitHub issue. Use Dismiss Feedback Acknowledgement or Escape to close the message.

Cloud sandbox conversations can show previously loaded messages while refreshing silently. If recent messages cannot be loaded, use Tab to reach Refresh in the banner and press Enter or Space. Refresh retries recorded history without restarting the session, waking its environment, or sending your draft.

When another Codex app is using a conversation, a banner above the input explains how to release it. You can keep editing your draft, but sending is disabled. Quit the app holding the conversation, such as ChatGPT, or exit the Codex CLI session. Use Tab to focus Retry in the banner, then press Enter or Space to check again. Retry does not send your draft.
In the input box, inspect the last response in the accessible view{0}. Thinking content is included in order by default.
To include or exclude thinking content in the accessible view, run the Toggle Thinking Content in Accessible View command from the Command Palette.
Focus a link in the chat transcript and press Shift+F10 to open its context menu. Use Copy Link to copy its target. File links with additional editor choices also provide Open With.

When enterprise policy disables Local, it remains in the harness picker as a disabled option. Use Tab to reach its Learn why link and Enter to open policy guidance. Its hover also includes a Learn why Local is disabled link. Disabled options cannot be selected.

A model's detail page has a heading for each section; the first, the model's name, also gives the model's state, such as Ready or Downloading 41%. Its header has icon buttons named after the model; Tab reaches them and Left and Right Arrow move between them. The first shows the state and what it does: Load for a model that isn't loaded, which loads it right away; Resume while it is paused; Stop while it is loaded; and while the model is busy, an in-progress indicator named with the state and the action that stops it, such as Loading, Cancel, or Downloading 41%, Pause, or Cancel while a model change waits for running responses, which keeps the loaded model. Once chosen, it reads Pausing, Cancelling or Stopping and can't be chosen again until the state changes. Then come Update, when an update is available, with its size, and Remove, which asks first. Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move between its links, buttons, choices and switches, Back to Models to return to the list, and Escape to close the picker. A warning at the top says when this device doesn't have the GPU memory for the model at its context size. To download a model, its page states the download size, the free space needed, the source and the license; choosing Download, or Set Up for model files already on this device, agrees to exactly what the page shows and downloads it in the background. Downloading doesn't need llama.cpp, but loading a model does, and VS Code doesn't install it. When no llama-server is set, or the one set doesn't support the model or is too old, loading the model shows an error on its page and in the notice above the chat input, with Get llama.cpp, which opens directions for getting a build that supports the model, Open Settings, which opens the Llama Server Path setting (chat.copilot.localModel.llamaServerPath) to point to its llama-server, and Retry. While a model downloads, its page shows a progress bar and the time remaining. While it loads, the page shows Loading model or Warming up, or Reloading when a new context size loads it again, or Retrying without speculative decoding, and why, when this llama.cpp build crashed with it, and, when an earlier load of the same model and context size took a known time, a progress bar and the time remaining estimated from it, which counts down and reads Almost done once that time has passed; a screen reader hears when the step changes. An installed model's page has an Effort Level choice when the model supports it, which sets its effort level for this chat, like a cloud model's effort level, without reloading it; the row and the readout show the new level. It also has a Context choice of the model's context sizes, each read with the GPU memory it needs. Changing the context size of a loaded model reloads it right away without asking, once its running responses finish; for a model that isn't loaded, it applies the next time it loads. In these choices, use the arrow keys to move between options, then Enter or Space to choose one. The page also has the Use in Auto switch, which lets Auto run some requests on this device with cloud fallback. The page updates in place as the model's state changes, and a change of state is announced.

While an on-device model is selected, the readout beside the model name in the chat input shows its state while it isn't ready, such as Loading, Reloading or Not loaded, and its effort level and context size once it is; a screen reader hears all of them, and the readout opens the model's detail page. On-device models show no notifications. Instead, one notice above the chat input shows an error, a running download, a model loading or reloading or another step with a progress bar and the busy indicator of an active session, or a pause, with its actions, such as the Pause, Cancel or Stop Now button, Retry, Resume or Review, which opens the model's detail page; use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach them. The notice has no Details action: the model's detail page opens from the readout or the model picker. A load's progress is estimated from the last comparable load, with a time remaining that counts down on screen and then reads almost done; the first load shows no estimate. After Pause, Cancel or Stop Now, the notice says Pausing, Cancelling or Stopping right away, and so does the button, which can't be chosen again. While a selected model waits for the loaded model's running responses, the notice says how many it waits for, with Stop Now, which asks first, and Cancel, which keeps the loaded model; a load always has Cancel. For a screen reader its text updates are throttled, and it hears when the step changes, pauses or fails. When an on-device model is ready, the same notice offers to switch to it. Use in Auto is off until you turn it on in the model's detail page, where its description also says that local models may not use the same safety filters as GitHub Copilot-provided models. With Auto selected and Use in Auto on, Auto may run some requests on this device and uses a cloud model when the device can't respond; a reply that ran on this device shows On-device after the model name, and a notice tells you the first time a cloud model was used instead in a chat. The Command Palette also has Set Up On-Device Model, which opens the detail page of the model to set up, and Cancel On-Device Model Download, Resume On-Device Model Download, Retry On-Device Model Setup, Update On-Device Model, Remove On-Device Model, Start On-Device Model, Stop On-Device Model and Make On-Device Model Active.

On-device models: when this device has an NVIDIA GPU that can run one, the model picker lists it in its On This Device tab, right after the Copilot tab, in Copilot chats that run on the local agent host. From the model list, use Left and Right Arrow to switch tabs and Up and Down Arrow to focus a model's row. Each model has a single row, like a cloud model's: its name, an Active badge while it is loaded or loading, and the effort level and context size, such as Medium and 128K. A screen reader also reads the model's state while it isn't ready, such as Downloading 42% or Not loaded; the detail page and the notice above the chat input show it too. Tab reaches the row's only button, labelled with the model's effort level and context size, or, for a model that isn't downloaded, Download (Set Up for model files already on this device), the download's progress, such as 42%, or Paused; it opens the model's detail page; Right Arrow on the row opens it too. Actions such as Retry, Pause, Resume, Download and Set Up are on the detail page, and those for a running, paused or failed step also in the notice above the chat input. Pause stops a download or update so it can be resumed later; Cancel takes back a model change, keeping the loaded model while the change waits for running responses, or stops loading a model, and Stop Now ends the responses a model change is waiting for. Once chosen, these read Pausing, Cancelling or Stopping and can't be chosen again until the model's state changes. A model that isn't downloaded can't be selected: a screen reader reads Not downloaded with its row, and Enter opens its detail page, which has its license, size and Download button. Enter on an installed model selects it and starts loading it right away, without asking. Only one on-device model is loaded at a time: selecting another one unloads the loaded one once its running responses finish, and the notice above the chat input shows how many responses it is waiting for, then the load, with Cancel.

If loading your organization's managed settings fails, your request remains in the conversation. Use Tab to focus Retry below the error, then press Enter or Space to resend that request. While settings are loading, Stop cancels the pending request.
The same read and unread shortcuts work on nested sessions and change only the targeted nested sessions, not their parent.
When the Sessions list has focus, mark the focused session or selected sessions as read{0} or unread{1} without opening them. These shortcuts do not apply while typing in an input.

When a chat turn is waiting for MCP servers to start, a Skip link may appear. Use Tab to focus Skip and press Enter or Space to continue the turn while those servers start in the background. The current startup message disappears immediately and focus returns to the chat input. New server startups may show another message.

Connect to Mission Control Environment opens a list of existing user-local hosts. Cached hosts are shown while the list refreshes in the background without clearing your search. Use Up and Down Arrow to choose a host and Enter to connect, or Escape to cancel. The owning application must be running; connecting does not create replacement compute. Passive connections are read-only, and local sessions continue using the local host.

In the model picker, Auto is the first model in the Copilot tab and is selected like any other model. Provider tabs and search remain available. Browsing another provider does not change the selected model.

Model default means no effort override is selected; focusing an effort option does not select it. Use the arrow keys to focus an option and Enter or Space to choose it. Context Size shows selectable windows when available. A value prefixed with Max is the model's capacity, not a selected context window. New Cloud chat choices are checked against the host before the first request is sent.

In the model picker, effort level and context appear as a configuration button on the hovered, selected, or keyboard-focused model. Use Up and Down Arrow to focus a model and Enter to select it. To open its information and configuration page without selecting it, press Right Arrow, or use Tab to reach its configuration button and press Enter or Space. The button shows Details when no readout is available. Models without configurable settings still open their information page. The effort level and context readout beside the model name in the chat input opens the same page for the current model. Opening the page focuses its configuration controls when available. Known values are shown even at their defaults. The Back to Models arrow is beside the model name; navigation and model actions stay at the top while details scroll. Back to Models, or {0}, returns to the previous provider, search, and model list with focus on that model. Escape closes the picker from any page and restores focus.

When Auto's tiers come from the Copilot service, Auto is presented as Copilot Fusion, and its details hold an "Effort Level" setting instead, such as Standard, High, and Max. The selected effort level is described below the setting, and a Learn more link follows Copilot Fusion's description. Choosing an effort level keeps Copilot Fusion checked with that effort level.

HydraFusion, a research preview, is listed after Auto as a model of its own. When HydraFusion Max is available, HydraFusion's details offer two tiers, Default and Max, along with a Learn more link. Choosing one selects it and keeps HydraFusion's details open. HydraFusion stays in the model list with that tier as its readout, and the readout beside HydraFusion in the chat input opens the same details.

In the model picker, Org default identifies the model your organization sets for new chats. It remains on that model when you choose another model for this chat; the checkmark identifies your current selection. Auto carries the same label when it is the organization default.

An agent host can make effort level or context read-only. Its value is announced as managed by the agent host and cannot be changed. An overridable default remains selectable. Changing models uses the options available for the newly selected model.

Auto's details hold its "Optimize for" preference: Efficiency, Balance, or Intelligence. Open them from Auto like any model's details, then use arrow keys to move between preferences and Enter or Space to choose one. Choosing a preference selects Auto and keeps its details open. When Auto has a discount, it is described below the preferences. The preference readout beside Auto in the chat input opens the same details.

In the model picker, less common models are grouped under Other Models, which reports whether it is expanded. With Other Models focused, press Right Arrow or Enter to expand it. Press Left Arrow on Other Models or on any model in it to collapse it and return focus to Other Models.

Pricing Details expands in place without moving the model's controls. Expansion and collapse are immediate when reduced motion is enabled. If the details exceed the available space, use Page Up or Page Down while the model details have focus to scroll.
In the model picker, use {0} and {1} to switch to the next or previous provider tab. When a provider tab is focused, Left and Right Arrow also switch tabs.

In a model's details, use Tab to reach effort level, context, and model actions. Use arrow keys to move between options, then Enter or Space to choose one. Reset to Default appears beside Pin Model when effort level or context has been changed. It restores both settings to the model's defaults without changing its pinned state. Choosing an option or resetting the settings selects that model and keeps its details open. Pinning or unpinning updates the model list without moving its details or keyboard focus. Back does not undo saved settings, but a save that finishes after leaving details does not override a newer model selection.

Type while the model list is focused to search across all providers. In the search field, use Up and Down Arrow to navigate results, Enter to select a model, and Escape to close the picker. Left and Right Arrow move the text cursor.

When a subagent starts another subagent, its activity row identifies the nested subagent by name. Focus that link with Tab and press Enter or Space to open the nested subagent's chat to the side. The enclosing pill still opens the parent subagent.
When a chat question is focused, move to the next question{0}.

Open Agents Window brings an already-open window to the front without changing its active or visible sessions, unless the action explicitly requests a session or New Session. Revealing New Session preserves any unsent draft.

When retained full output is available for a completed command, use the View Full Output link below the output preview, or the Open Full Output (Read-Only) action in the command header or terminal output Accessible View, to open it in a read-only editor. You can also focus the output region and press Enter.
The quick chat view is comprised of an input box and a request/response list. The input box is used to make requests and the list is used to display responses.

Submitting an @ chat participant from an Agent Host chat starts a Local chat for that participant, preserving your message and attachments. The original conversation remains available. Your organization may restrict Local chats.
To paste the clipboard as plain text, without converting it to Markdown or storing it as an attachment, invoke Paste as Text{0}.

When Assisted permissions or Allow all is unavailable for a session, the option remains in the permissions picker as a disabled option with its reason, such as Disabled by policy when your organization's policy disables it. Its hover also explains the restriction. Disabled options cannot be selected.

The chat.experimental.persistentProgress setting defaults to Draw in all versions of VS Code. Experiments can override the default; an explicit setting takes precedence. Choose Draw, Draw (Monochrome), or Draw (Monochrome, No Icon) to keep a working progress indicator at the bottom until the response finishes. When the response finishes, its toolbar takes the indicator's place. Draw ties and unravels the VS Code mark with fast parabolic ribbon motion and a brief rest between loops. The No Icon variant hides only the decorative VS Code icon; progress text and spoken updates are unchanged. The chat.experimental.persistentProgressVerbosity setting defaults to Compact: tool calls preview while running, then collapse in place to a single summary row when thinking or response text resumes, or the response finishes. Choose Verbose to keep tool chains expanded without a group header or an internal scrolling limit. Choose Conversation to collapse reasoning and tool calls together into one section between response text; the section starts collapsed, its header names the current tool call, or the heading of the current reasoning summary (Thinking when the reasoning has no heading), while it runs, and reports how long it took once it finishes, such as Finished thinking after 5s, or Finished thinking when the time is unknown. Use Tab to focus a summary and press Enter or Space to expand or collapse its tool calls. Automatic collapse waits until keyboard focus leaves the group. Completed responses still follow chat.agent.collapseCompletedResponses. Except in Conversation, reasoning appears separately as collapsible previews; focus a reasoning header and press Enter or Space to expand or collapse it. Standalone tools keep their decorative icons. Terminal activity animations and subagent pills are unchanged. The indicator reports counts of running subagents and background commands, including work started in earlier requests, whether the main response is progressing or idle. Requests for your input, approval, plan review, or authentication take priority over these counts. After 90 seconds without response activity and with no active tools, progress tasks, or known background work, it reports that the response is taking longer than usual. Long-running foreground terminal commands do not trigger this message. Reduced motion disables the collapse animation and the Conversation header's transitions between steps, and keeps the indicator visible without animation. Spoken progress updates are controlled by accessibility.verboseChatProgressUpdates.

While a response is running, automatically collapsing a reasoning or tool preview keeps a visible header in place. If the header is above the visible content but its details are visible, it moves below the pinned prompt, or to the top of the viewport when there is no pinned prompt. Only the space needed for the visible viewport is reserved. That space is removed when the response finishes or is stopped, after any pending transition and content rendering finish. Expanding a preview consumes reserved space as its content grows. Scrolling to the bottom removes the reserved space. Manual collapses do not add padding. The following response content appears after an automatic collapse finishes. Reduced motion skips this delay. If keyboard focus keeps a preview open, new content continues to appear without waiting for focus to move.

With Compact persistent progress, a single tool uses its normal rendering, icon, and details without a group summary or automatic group collapse. Group headers summarize up to three activity groups from Agent Host data, prioritizing edits and commands, without an additional model request. Remaining activity is counted as other steps; this counts tool calls and visible steps rather than unique files or search phrases. Expand the summary to inspect all calls. Repeated files and search phrases are counted once in named activity groups. Read summaries count files rather than requested lines. Edit summaries show filenames or file counts, with available additions and deletions in the existing diff badge. Failed, skipped, denied, and unfinished tool invocations remain explicit, including when folded into other steps. A completed shell invocation counts as a command even if its process continues in the background; group headers do not track later process status. Groups with no recognized activity or outcome retain a neutral step-count summary. MCP tools use the MCP icon. The working indicator reports when chat is waiting for your answers instead of showing a separate question-tool progress row. Question controls remain available, answered questions remain in the response, and question-tool failures remain visible.

With persistent progress, reasoning headers say Thinking while content arrives. When reasoning finishes, a single heading becomes the header and is removed from the details. Multiple headings remain in the details, with a summary in the header when chat.agent.thinking.generateTitles is enabled and title generation is available. Otherwise, the header says Finished thinking, followed by how long it took when that is known.

When a plan is ready for review, open it from the chat response to edit the plan and add line comments. Use the editor toolbar to navigate, clear, or submit feedback. Choose an implementation action from the plan review in Chat.

If your organization configures managed permissions or requires sandboxing, opening an existing Local chat automatically moves its conversation and draft to Copilot without sending. The original chat is archived only after the new conversation opens with its history. If moving fails, the original stays read-only. Use Tab to focus Move to Copilot in the banner, then press Enter or Space to try again. Archived originals remain available without moving again, and in remote windows they still offer Move to Copilot so you can recover chats that an earlier move archived without copying their history. Empty chats offer New Copilot Chat instead. When the Agent Host cannot import history, nothing moves automatically. Use Tab to focus Continue in Copilot in the banner, then press Enter or Space to start a new Copilot chat with the conversation attached as context and your draft, without sending. The original chat stays available and is not archived, and archived chats offer this too.
When a chat question is focused, move to the previous question{0}.

As the chat request is being processed, you will hear verbose progress updates if the request takes more than 4 seconds. This includes information like searched text for <search term> with X results, created file <file_name>, or read file <file path>. This can be disabled with accessibility.verboseChatProgressUpdates.

In read-only chats, thinking details preview while streaming and collapse when finished, regardless of your thinking-style setting. Focus a thinking header and press Enter or Space to expand or collapse its details.

If you have bring your own key (BYOK) models configured and select Copilot on a connected remote host, the first eligible chat input in this editor window shows a warning that these models are not supported. The warning does not repeat in other chats in the same window. Use Tab to reach Dismiss notification or Don't Show Again, then Enter or Space to activate it. Dismiss notification hides the warning until the window reloads. Don't Show Again permanently hides this warning for your profile, including when new models are added.

On desktop, Remote Connections is available in the local Agent Host chat toolbar or the Agents window title bar. The preview setting chat.agentHost.remoteConnections selects the connection method. The Remote Connections button opens a menu that offers Off, Dev Tunnels, and GitHub Environments when available. Use Tab to reach the button in chat or arrow keys in the title bar, Enter or Space to open it, Up and Down Arrow to choose an option, Enter to select, and Escape to close and return focus to the button. Selecting a method updates the setting and enables sharing. Selecting Off disables sharing without changing the preferred method. The footer shows the name used to identify this machine on other clients and whether it is shared or connecting. Changing the setting directly turns sharing off. The setting chat.agentHost.githubEnvironments.enabled controls GitHub Environments availability. If your organization disables it, the menu explains that you must contact your administrator. With GitHub environment selected, enabling sharing registers your local environment for remote owner access. Remote work uses the host's OAuth token by default, controlled by chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControl.useLocalCredentials. Local sessions continue using local IPC.

If GitHub Environments is disabled by your organization, the footer explains the restriction. Press Tab to reach View Setting and Enter to open the managed setting. Shift+Tab returns to the connection options.

In the Remote Connections menu, press Tab to reach the name link in the footer, then Enter or Space to rename the shared environment. The input starts with the current name. Enter saves the name shown on other clients, and Escape cancels. Shift+Tab returns to the connection options. Renaming while Off does not enable sharing.
To rename the current chat session when supported, invoke the Rename command{0}. Agent Host sessions can be renamed after sending the first request.
In the input box, use up and down arrows to navigate your request history. Edit input and use enter or the submit button to run a new request.

To open an image shown in a response, use Tab to focus it and press Enter or Space. To attach it to your next request, open its context menu{0} and choose Add File to Chat, or drag it into the chat input.

Open the Command Palette{0} and run Sandbox: Manage Trusted CA for the last-focused chat. Use Up and Down Arrow to choose Install, Rotate, or Remove, then Enter to continue or Escape to cancel. If there is no agent-host target for the last-focused chat, a dialog says No agent host detected.

Use Tab to reach Learn more for certificate guidance. When the host supports certificate installation, use Tab to reach the Install button and Enter or Space to activate it. You can also choose Install in Manage Trusted CA after dismissing the notice. A confirmation names the host. Install creates and trusts the certificate, replacing it if needed. Running tools may need to restart. Progress appears in the notice; failures are shown in a dialog.

If the agent host reports a missing sandbox certificate that it can install, an informational notice appears above the focused chat input. Installation is optional and chatting is not blocked. Dependency warnings take priority over this notice. Use Tab to reach Dismiss notification and Enter or Space to hide certificate notices for that host runtime in this window.

Choose Remove in Manage Trusted CA to remove OS trust. The stored certificate authority is kept. A confirmation explains that tools relying on OS trust may stop working. Progress appears in the notice; completion and failures are shown in a dialog.

Choose Rotate in Manage Trusted CA to replace the installed sandbox CA and private key. A confirmation explains that the CA is shared and running tools may need to restart. Progress appears in the notice; completion and failures are shown in a dialog.

When a sandbox confirmation offers path access, review the granted path and whether it allows reading or reading and writing. A grant may cover a folder rather than only the blocked file. The header asks to add access to user sandbox settings and retry. Allow saves access in your user settings and retries inside the sandbox. These settings are shared with connected agent hosts across workspaces and sessions. Skip declines access. Use Tab to reach these choices.

If the agent host cannot support the configured sandbox, a notification above the input explains why. You can select and copy the warning text. Use Tab to reach support links or Dismiss notification, and Enter to open a focused link. Dismissing hides the warning for this session until the window reloads, without changing sandboxing or preventing messages.

Select text within an assistant response and open the context menu with Shift+F10 or the context menu key. Choose Ask in Side Chat... to open a small Ask Question input. Type a question and press Enter to open a side chat with conversation context through the selected response and its quoted text. Escape closes the input and returns focus to the response. Asking requires a writable conversation that supports side chats.

Subagents and Customizations are available in both the Agents Window and editor window, and are hidden by default. Enable them from the session status toolbar context menu. Subagents lists the current chat's direct subagents, grouped into in-progress and completed chats. Activate an entry to open its chat to the side. Subagent Options lets you show all subagents or only those in progress, remembered across windows. Customizations lists the agents, skills, instructions, hooks, prompts, MCP servers, and plugins used by the current chat. Activate an entry to reveal it in the Customizations editor.

An archive suggestion appears above the chat input when the session's pull requests are merged. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach Archive, Configure Automatic Cleanup, or Dismiss Archive Suggestion, then press Enter or Space. Configure Automatic Cleanup opens the settings for automatically archiving inactive merged sessions and permanently deleting automatically archived merged sessions. The explanation under What Does "Archive" Do? is collapsed by default. Use Tab to reach it and Enter or Space to expand or collapse it. Dismissing the suggestion, including with Escape while it is focused, returns to the chat input. Archiving the session hides it from the sessions list so you can focus on your remaining tasks. The session is not deleted. Ask your agent to find it, or look in the "Archived" section of the sessions list. You can unarchive it anytime. The worktree created for the session, if any, will be deleted. You can recreate it by unarchiving the session.

A mark as done suggestion appears above the chat input when the session's pull requests are merged. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach Mark as Done, Configure Automatic Cleanup, or Dismiss Mark as Done Suggestion, then press Enter or Space. Configure Automatic Cleanup opens the settings for automatically archiving inactive merged sessions and permanently deleting automatically archived merged sessions. The explanation under What Does "Mark as Done" Do? is collapsed by default. Use Tab to reach it and Enter or Space to expand or collapse it. Dismissing the suggestion, including with Escape while it is focused, returns to the chat input. Marking the session as done hides it from the sessions list so you can focus on your remaining tasks. The session is not deleted. Ask your agent to find it, or look in the "Done" section of the sessions list. You can restore it anytime. The worktree created for the session, if any, will be deleted. You can recreate it by restoring the session.

While a session is being prepared, a progress message appears in the transcript. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach Show Log, when available, and press Enter or Space to open the output log. Use Stop to cancel preparation. The chat input and attachment controls are disabled until preparation finishes.
In the Pull Requests pill, open the dropdown and use a pull request's Open Pull Request Changes row action to view its changed files in a multi-file diff editor.

When a pill represents a single item, its context menu offers the item's copy actions, such as copying its URL or file path. For a collection, open the dropdown and use the individual row actions instead.

When session status pills appear above the input, use Tab to focus the toolbar, then use the left and right arrow keys to move between pills. Press Enter or Space to activate a pill. An aggregated pill opens a picker. Use Pin on a picker row to keep that entry as its own pill; it is removed from the picker, and a sole remaining entry is shown directly unless it requires a details picker. A pinned pill shows a trailing Unpin button that pointer users can activate to unpin it. Keyboard and screen reader users can open the pinned pill's context menu{0} and choose Unpin. Pin choices are remembered for each chat. The context menu also lets you choose which optional pills are visible. Pull Requests Options lets you show all pull requests or only open and draft ones, remembered across sessions. If every pull request is filtered out, these options are also available in any other pill's context menu or the toolbar context menu.

When space is limited, session status pills collapse to icons one at a time from right to left. Their full labels remain available to screen readers and in tooltips. Labels return as space becomes available. If the icons still do not fit, the row scrolls horizontally; use the arrow keys to reach every pill.

The working set above the input lists changes across the whole session instead of showing a Changes pill. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach its heading and press Enter or Space to expand or collapse it. {0} Use Tab to reach the file list, Up and Down Arrow to choose a file, and Enter to open it in a regular editor at its first edit. Each file announces its path and added and removed line counts.

Press Shift+F10 or the Context Menu key on the working set heading or a file to open its context menu. Keep and Undo is checked by default; toggle it to show or hide review controls in both the working set and open editors. View All Edits remains available. Show Pill replaces the working set with the Changes pill by turning off chat.editor.workingSet.enabled. The Changes pill's context menu offers Show Working Set to restore it.

To keep or undo the session's changes to the chosen file, or open them in a diff editor, press Tab to reach its Keep button, Left and Right Arrow to move between Keep, Undo, and Open Changes in Diff Editor, and Enter or Space to activate one. Keep removes files from the working set until the session changes them again, as does staging or committing them with Git. Undo reverts the session's changes after any confirmation the session asks for, and deletes a file the session created. Undo is available only when the session supports it, and is unavailable while a request is running. The accessibility.signals.editsKept and accessibility.signals.editsUndone settings control the signals played when changes are kept or undone.

To keep the session's changes to the chosen file, or open them in a diff editor, press Tab to reach its Keep button, Left and Right Arrow to move between Keep and Open Changes in Diff Editor, and Enter or Space to activate one. Keep removes files from the working set until the session changes them again, as does staging or committing them with Git. The accessibility.signals.editsKept setting controls the signal played when changes are kept.
To inspect the chosen file's changes, press Tab to reach Open Changes in Diff Editor, then Enter or Space.
The Keep and View All Edits buttons after the heading keep the changes to every file in the working set, or open all of them in a diff editor.

The Keep, Undo, and View All Edits buttons after the heading keep or undo the changes to every file in the working set, or open all of them in a diff editor. Undo in the heading asks for confirmation.
The View All Edits button after the heading opens all changed files in a diff editor. Keep and Undo are hidden in both the working set and the editor.
If there are any hidden chat terminals, you can view them by invoking the View Hidden Chat Terminals command{0}.
Accessibility Signals can be changed via settings with a prefix of signals.chat. By default, if a request takes more than 4 seconds, you will hear a sound indicating that progress is still occurring.
To choose a microphone or turn off dictation or Voice Mode, focus the microphone button in the input toolbar and open its context menu{0} (for example Shift+F10).
The prompt you have scrolled past is pinned to the top of the transcript. Activate its title to jump back to that prompt.
When a subagent pill appears in a response, use Tab to focus it and press Enter or Space to open that subagent chat to the side.

Subagents appear as pills in the response. Use Tab to focus a subagent pill, then Enter or Space to open its chat to the side. If the subagent has no separate chat, Enter or Space expands or collapses its inline details instead. The pill announces its running state, model settings, and any pending confirmations. File and markdown links in its activity row can be focused with Tab and opened independently with Enter.
Some session status messages have additional details. Use Tab to focus the status message and press Enter or Space to show or hide its details.
Terminal output reflows to fit the chat width by default. Set {0} to false to keep fixed-width previews with horizontal scrolling. This only changes the preview, not the terminal running the command.

Failed tool calls use an error icon in place of their normal tool icon. Their content and available actions stay the same. The Accessible View includes the failure reason or terminal exit code when available.

When the experimental agents.voice.agentProgress setting is enabled, Voice Mode Agent requests may speak brief progress updates while investigating, planning, editing, validating, or recovering from a problem.

In manual Voice Mode, the Start or Stop Listening button toggles listening when tapped, or you can press and hold it to talk and release to send. You can also hold the Voice Mode: Hold to Talk keybinding{0} to talk and release to send; this interrupts the assistant to barge in.

When the segmented voice input control is enabled, the input toolbar offers Dictation and Voice Mode. A connected hands-free session also offers Mute or Unmute Microphone; manual Voice Mode instead offers Start or Stop Listening, where stopping sends the completed turn. Each button can be focused and activated with Enter or Space.

In OpenAI BYOK Voice Mode, say approve, approved, accept, accepted, allow, yes, I approve, or I accept to approve the current prompt, and reject, deny, or no to reject it. These approval commands must be complete, unqualified English replies. For questions, say an exact displayed choice or its number; for multiple selections, separate choices with commas or and. Answer text questions directly. To give a custom answer to a selection question that permits it, say other followed by your answer. Forms collect one answer at a time and submit when complete. Say skip only when the form permits skipping. Ambiguous replies ask for clarification without approving anything or sending a new chat request.

When using configured OpenAI BYOK Voice Mode, only the bound chat input's prompts and responses are read. Voice Mode belongs to the input where you start it, including chat editor tabs and the chat sidebar. Switching the bound input or discarding a recording stops Voice Mode to prevent buffered audio from acting on another session. Start Voice Mode again in the intended input; creating the session from the same draft does not require a restart.

The first time Voice Mode starts, an introduction appears above the input box. Tab to reach it, then use the arrow keys to move between the available voices; Enter or Space plays a voice and keeps it for future conversations. Its description also contains two links: Settings, which opens the Voice Mode settings, and How It Responds, which opens a file for customizing what the agent says back. Voice Mode stays connected but does not listen while the introduction is open. Press Escape, or activate the Close button, to dismiss it and return to the input box.
For forms with multiple questions, Voice Mode identifies the current question by number. Answer only that question, then wait for the next one. Each spoken reply fills one field, not several fields.

When agents.voice.sessionAwareness is enabled, OpenAI BYOK Voice Mode receives a bounded session briefing and the active chat's recent conversation. You can ask where you left off, what just happened, or which tracked session needs input without starting a coding request. The briefing may not include every session. Coding work and replies to approvals still use the bound chat input. Disable the setting and reconnect Voice Mode to restore input-only context.

When Voice Mode sends a new request while the coding agent is working, it is sent as steering rather than queued for after the current task. Voice-only exchanges during ongoing work are not retained as context for later requests. Answers to pending questions and approvals continue to respond to those prompts.

Type /vscode-pet to show or hide Blobby, the VS Code pet, above the input. One pet appears in whichever editor or Agents window is active. Drag it around the chat with the mouse and release it to drop it, or flick it in any direction to throw it along the gesture before gravity pulls it down. Pointer collisions are ignored for half a second after a drag release. After that, while the pet is falling, move the pointer into it to bounce it upward; pointer movement and where it catches the pet affect the bounce. Sideways and upward travel do not start the bounce counter. A counter beside the pet tracks consecutive bounces and remains for up to five seconds after landing, or until the pet next reacts or interacts. Landing with at least twenty bounces triggers confetti unless reduced motion is enabled. If it falls past the input, a despawn effect appears at the bottom and a respawn effect appears at the top before it automatically returns to the input. Moving the pointer rapidly between the pet’s left and right sides makes it dizzy. With the keyboard, use Tab to focus the pet, then the left and right arrows to make it hop along the input until it reaches an edge. Hold Shift with the left or right arrow to throw it toward a wall; while it is airborne, press Enter or Space to bounce it upward. Rapidly alternate the unmodified arrows to make it dizzy. Press Enter or Space while it is resting to interact with it. When an achievement unlocks, the pet shows a gold star for ten seconds; activate the pet during that time to open Achievements. Open its context menu{0} (for example Shift+F10), use the up and down arrow keys to choose Achievements, Go on the Run, Come Back, Grow, Shrink, Reset Size, or Change Color, and press Enter to activate the choice. Grow and Shrink change its size in twenty-percent steps, while Reset Size restores its default size. The pet position, size, and color are shared across chats and windows and remembered after you restart.
While an image-generation tool is running, Blobby paints at a small easel, then returns to its normal activity. Reduced motion shows a still painting pose.

When the experimental combined picker is enabled for a Copilot Agent Host session or a new Cloud session, Tab reaches separate Mode and Permissions buttons. Press Enter or Space on Mode to open the picker with Agent Mode expanded, or on Permissions to open it with Permissions expanded. Each section header shows its current selection, and the opened section initially focuses that selection. Press Enter or Space on a section header to expand or collapse it, or use Right Arrow to expand and Left Arrow to collapse. Hover or keyboard navigation moves the single row highlight without changing the selection until you activate a choice. Focus the Permissions header and press Tab to reach Configure Permissions, which opens the related settings. Use Up and Down Arrow to navigate and Enter to select a mode, permission level, or terminal sandboxing. Assisted permissions is experimental and evaluates risk before running tools. When Assisted permissions or Allow all is unavailable for a session, the option remains visible but cannot be selected, with a reason such as Disabled by policy. Its hover also explains the restriction. When the session's host requires terminal sandboxing, its sandbox toggle is checked and disabled. If your organization permits bypassing, a supported outside-sandbox permission prompt can offer Allow in this Session. After that action succeeds, you can use the toggle to enable sandboxing again. This restriction applies only to that session. Cloud draft choices are locked while the first request starts the session. Escape closes the picker and returns focus to the button that opened it.

Global auto approve also known as "YOLO mode" disables manual approval completely for _all tools in all workspaces_, allowing the agent to act fully autonomously. This is extremely dangerous and is *never* recommended, even containerized environments like [Codespaces](https://github.com/features/codespaces) and [Dev Containers](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers) have user keys forwarded into the container that could be compromised.

**This feature disables [critical security protections](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/security) and makes it much easier for an attacker to compromise the machine.**
